title: Merged optimization targets
description: Output of the merge phase: deduplicated optimization targets ready for the optimizer fan-out, plus per-family lens dispositions for the summary phase. Each accepted analysis may emit multiple targets; merge dedups across the flat union of all analyzer-emitted targets. Convergence across analyses (multiple distinct families landing on the same structural change) is high-confidence signal that the target is real.

merge_method.description: Identifier of which merge implementation produced this output. Reserved for future expansion if alternative merge implementations are added; currently only `llm` exists.

merge_model.description: The exact model identifier used for the merge call (e.g. 'gpt-5.3-codex-spark', 'gpt-5.3-codex'). Empty string only for the no-op empty-input case.

rejected_by_merge.description: Analyzer-emitted targets the merger affirmatively dropped (rare; e.g., recognized as already-shipped, scope-out reasons). Coverage invariant: every analyzer-emitted target (identified by `{family_id, target_index}`) must appear in EXACTLY ONE of: a merged target's `merged_from`, OR this list.

target_index.description: Zero-based index into the source analysis's `targets[]` array.

lens_dispositions.description: Per-family lens dispositions, propagated from each accepted analysis's `lens_disposition` field. Independent of `targets[]`: a family with `status == "not_actionable"` and zero opportunistic targets contributes 0 entries to `targets` and 0 to `rejected_by_merge` but still appears here. Used by the summary phase to surface 'real hotspot, no fix found' cases. Coverage invariant: every accepted family_id appears here exactly once.

allOf.description: When status == 'not_actionable', the operator-facing explanation MUST be preserved. The whole point of this branch is to record why a real hotspot has no fix; dropping the reason would defeat the purpose.

id.description: Canonical kebab-case identifier; equal to the canonical fix_signature of this target group. Used as a path segment (experiments/<id>/) by Phase 2 onward.

merged_from.description: References to the analyzer-emitted targets that contributed to this merged target. Each entry identifies a specific target within a specific analysis by `(family_id, target_index)`. A given `(family_id, target_index)` pair must NEVER appear in two different merged targets, and two targets within the same analysis cannot collapse into one merged target (intra-analysis merge is forbidden — those are distinct findings the analyzer chose to keep separate).

target_index.description: Zero-based index into the source analysis's `targets[]` array.

convergence_count.description: Length of `merged_from`. Higher = more analyzer-emitted targets agreed on this fix = higher confidence. With multi-target analyses, convergence across DISTINCT family_ids is the stronger signal — note in `merge_notes` if convergence comes from different targets within fewer families.

rank.description: Optional priority ordering hint for the optimizer fan-out.

bucket.description: Carried through from the contributing analyzer-emitted targets. All entries in `merged_from` must reference targets with the same bucket — the merge prompt forbids cross-bucket merges.

total_wall_us.description: Inclusive wall time of the target span. Required for parity with analysis.schema.json's hotspot requirement; the merge phase carries this through from the contributing targets.

evidence.description: Canonical synthesis. When merging multiple targets, the merger should preserve the strongest evidence from each contributor.

proposed_change.description: Canonical version of the change. When contributors phrased the change differently, the merger picks the most concrete and actionable wording.

expected_improvement.description: Per-axis percent-reduction estimates merged from contributors. Per-axis median when N >= 2 contributors (see merge prompt's canonicalization rules). Same shape as analysis.schema.json's analyzer_target.expected_improvement.

merge_notes.description: Optional reviewer-facing note from the merger: why these targets were collapsed, what was preserved, what was canonicalized.

contributor_differences.description: Optional: short bullets describing where contributors disagreed (different files cited, slightly different fix wording, > 50% spread on any axis of expected_improvement). Useful for reviewers spot-checking the merge quality.

consensus_breaking.description: Carried through from the contributing analyzer-emitted targets. All entries in `merged_from` must reference targets with the same `consensus_breaking` value — the merge prompt forbids cross-class merges. See analysis.schema.json analyzer_target.consensus_breaking for full semantics.

breakage_class.description: Required when `consensus_breaking == true`. Carried from contributors; all contributors to a consensus-breaking merged target must share the same breakage_class.

poc_implementable.description: Required when `consensus_breaking == true`. Canonicalized via the conservative rule: if any contributor has `false`, the merged target gets `false` (the safer routing).

poc_test_scope.description: Required when `poc_implementable == true`. Canonicalized as the union of all contributors' scopes, deduplicated.

consensus_writeup.description: Required when `consensus_breaking == true`. Canonicalized to the most detailed contributor's writeup; differences flagged in contributor_differences.

delivery_mode.description: Derived field set by the merge phase from `consensus_breaking` + `poc_implementable`. Routes the target through the rest of the pipeline: `normal_pr` follows the existing optimizer + benchmark + PR flow; `consensus_poc_pr` runs a scoped optimizer (no benchmark) and produces a draft PR labeled to prevent merging; `consensus_issue` skips the optimizer entirely and the publisher creates a GitHub issue from `consensus_writeup`. Derivation: false→`normal_pr`; true+true→`consensus_poc_pr`; true+false→`consensus_issue`.

bench_eligible.description: Derived field set by the merge phase: true iff `delivery_mode == "normal_pr"`. bench-experiments.sh filters on this; consensus-breaking targets are skipped (the bench harness encodes current-epoch consensus and would either crash or produce meaningless numbers under a consensus change).

allOf.description: When consensus_breaking == true, breakage_class + poc_implementable + consensus_writeup are required at the merged-target level too.
When poc_implementable == true, poc_test_scope is required and non-empty.

block_validation is NOT exercised by stacks-bench's mining harness — PoC mode cannot prove correctness via the bench regardless of test scope. Mirrored from analysis.schema.json so the constraint survives the merge phase even when contributors disagree.
poc_test_scope is allowed ONLY when poc_implementable == true.
Non-consensus merged targets must not carry consensus-only fields. Mirrored from analysis.schema.json so the constraint survives the merge phase.
delivery_mode derivation: consensus_breaking == true && poc_implementable == true → delivery_mode == "consensus_poc_pr".
delivery_mode derivation: consensus_breaking == true && poc_implementable == false → delivery_mode == "consensus_issue".
bench_eligible derivation: true iff delivery_mode == normal_pr.
